stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy intern works 11 creditable hours on Monday and 13 creditable hours on Tuesday at an approved training site. Ignoring any other requirements, what is the maximum internship credit that can be recorded for those two days under the daily-credit rule?

choices.text: 24 hours, because all time physically worked must be credited.
23 hours: Monday contributes 11 hours and Tuesday is capped at 12 hours.
22 hours, because every internship day is limited to exactly 11 hours.
12 hours total, because the daily cap also operates as a two-day cap.
Zero hours for Tuesday, because exceeding 12 hours of work voids all credit for that day.

explanation.core_reasoning: The Massachusetts rule limits internship credit to no more than 12 hours in a single day. Monday’s 11 hours remain creditable, while Tuesday contributes at most 12 of the 13 hours, producing 23 total creditable hours.

choice_analysis.A: Physical work beyond the daily credit ceiling does not increase the credit recorded for that day.
choice_analysis.B: Applying the cap separately to each day yields 11 plus 12 creditable hours.
choice_analysis.C: The rule sets a maximum rather than requiring every day to be reduced to 11 hours.
choice_analysis.D: The 12-hour ceiling is daily; it is not a multi-day aggregate ceiling.
choice_analysis.E: Working beyond the credit ceiling limits the recorded credit but does not make the entire day worth zero under the cited rule.

related_facts: A credit limit is not necessarily an employment-shift limit.
Daily caps must be applied to each calendar day before totals are combined.
explanation.mpje_trap: Apply the 12-hour ceiling day by day rather than subtracting hours from the entire multi-day period.

reasoning_steps: Apply the daily credit ceiling independently to Monday
Apply the same ceiling independently to Tuesday
